figure_caption: Study design and observation boundary. Addition and subtraction modulo 97 are independently trained under a shared fixed-rate MLP protocol crossing three hidden widths, two AdamW weight-decay settings, and three initialization seeds, defining 36 configurations. The operation-specific split is fixed across conditions; held-out examples supply measurements, never gradients. Fitting (memorization) requires training accuracy of at least 99%; generalization requires held-out accuracy of at least 95%, each for three consecutive checkpoints, timestamped at the first checkpoint and confirmed by the next two. Event-reporting branches are methodological alternatives, not empirical outcomes. Non-attainment at 20,000 updates is administrative censoring, not a measured generalization delay. The diagram summarizes the design, not a proposed neural circuit.

panels.title: Factorial design
panels.short_caption: Both operations cross every width, decay setting, and initialization seed; the grid defines 36 independently trained configurations.

panels.title: Shared protocol
panels.short_caption: A fixed operation-specific split feeds a trainable one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP; full-batch AdamW uses a constant learning rate, while held-out data supply measurements only.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: all factorial configurations share one fixed partition and optimization protocol, excluding held-out data from gradient updates.
Stable nodes and regions: retained is a sharp fixed-data box '4,705 pairs / task'; split is a fixed rounded preprocessing block 'Fixed hash split'; train is a sharp fixed-data box 'Training' with '1,411 pairs'; holdout is a sharp fixed-data box 'Held-out' with '3,294 pairs'. model is a rounded trainable-model container titled 'Trainable MLP', enclosing an ordered vertical chain: encoding is a fixed input strip 'One-hot pair' with '194 inputs'; hidden is a trainable rounded layer block 'ReLU hidden layer' with 'Width 16 / 64 / 256'; logits is a trainable rounded output layer '97 logits'. Hidden represents a biased linear layer plus ReLU and logits the second biased linear layer; do not draw neuron circuitry. loss is a rounded training-objective block 'Full-batch cross-entropy'; optimizer is a rounded parameter-update process 'AdamW' with '$$\eta=0.01$$'. train_measure and held_measure are sharp measurement-output tags 'Training accuracy' and 'Held-out accuracy', not empirical result values. schedule is a fixed metadata strip with '20,000 updates' and 'Checkpoints: every 500'.
Solid edges, all unlabelled except where specified: retained → split; split → train; split → holdout; train → encoding; holdout → encoding labelled 'Measurement only'; encoding → hidden; hidden → logits; logits → loss labelled 'Training only'; logits → train_measure; logits → held_measure. Dashed auxiliary/gradient edges: loss → optimizer unlabelled; optimizer → model labelled 'Parameter update'. The two measurement outputs correspond to the two subsets traversing the same model, not to separate models. Only training predictions enter loss. There is no held-out loss or held-out optimizer edge.
Layout: retained and split top-center; train and holdout in a two-column row below; model centrally beneath those. Route held-out input in a distinct outer side lane away from optimizer. Place measurement tags adjacent below model, training tag on the training side and held-out tag on the held-out side. Place loss and optimizer below those with a short auxiliary return path to model along the training-side margin. Put schedule at bottom. No arrows to other panels.
Importance: partition and training-versus-held-out roles first, trainable model and optimizer loop second, common schedule third.

panels.title: Events and censoring
panels.short_caption: Separate sustained-event definitions distinguish fitting from generalization. Generalization non-attainment at the fixed horizon is right-censored, not an observed delay; branches show alternative reporting states rather than results.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: fitting and generalization are distinct sustained events, and the observation endpoint is not a substitute generalization event. Draw methodological rules, never empirical accuracy plots.
Stable nodes and regions: fit_rule is a fixed-rule rounded card titled 'Fitting / memorization', carrying 'Training ≥99%' and an event tag '$$T_M$$'; gen_rule is a matching fixed-rule rounded card titled 'Generalization', carrying 'Held-out ≥95%' and event tag '$$T_G$$'. Each card contains exactly three adjacent outlined square checkpoint glyphs: fit_c1, fit_c2, fit_c3 and gen_c1, gen_c2, gen_c3. Every square contains the same checkmark, representing a hypothetical qualifying window, not recorded outcomes. shared_rule is a grouping annotation spanning both cards, '3 consecutive checkpoints'. timestamp_note is a two-part annotation below their grouping, 'Timestamp: first checkpoint' and 'Confirmation: next two'. Lower reporting region: horizon is a fixed observation-boundary header '$$H=20{,}000$$ updates'; decision is a diamond fixed reporting rule 'Generalization by H?'; attained is a sharp conditional-report box 'Observed event' with '$$T_G$$'; censored is a sharp conditional-report box 'Right-censored' with 'Non-attainment by H'; warning is a sharp caution callout below censored, 'No measured delay'. Report boxes are alternative methodological states, not empirical outcomes and not trainable objects.
Edges: gen_rule → decision is solid unlabelled event-reporting flow, routed outside timestamp annotations; decision → attained is solid labelled 'Yes'; decision → censored is solid labelled 'No'; censored → warning is dashed auxiliary interpretation, unlabelled. No edge connects fitting to generalization: a fitting event does not cause or establish generalization. Place horizon above decision as its observation boundary, without a horizon-as-event arrow.
Layout: stack fit_rule and gen_rule as equally prominent horizontal cards in the upper region; align their three checkpoint squares identically. Place shared_rule and timestamp_note together beneath both cards. Below, put horizon above decision, attained bottom-left and censored bottom-right, warning under censored. Attach event tags to their own criteria; leave clear whitespace between definitions and reporting logic.
Importance: separate training versus held-out thresholds first, checkpoint persistence and censoring warning second, branching details third.
Exact text budget: title 'Events and censoring'; 'Fitting / memorization'; 'Training ≥99%'; '$$T_M$$'; 'Generalization'; 'Held-out ≥95%'; '$$T_G$$'; six checkmarks; '3 consecutive checkpoints'; 'Timestamp: first checkpoint'; 'Confirmation: next two'; '$$H=20{,}000$$ updates'; 'Generalization by H?'; 'Yes'; 'No'; 'Observed event'; one repeated '$$T_G$$' in attained; 'Right-censored'; 'Non-attainment by H'; 'No measured delay'. Do not add accuracy curves, a time axis, measured T_M/T_G values, a future transition, capped-lag formulas, or palette prescriptions.
